text:
maya: quick question — noticed a bunch of logs coming into Loki without trace_id after the new OTLP collector rollout. seems like the collector is dropping attributes on some spans when exporter batches.

samir: ugh. which exporter? OTLP/gRPC to our ingest or the internal span-forwarder?

maya: internal span-forwarder. happens when spans are sampled out and we rely on the collector to enrich logs with trace_id via resource/baggage.

anna_k: are the logs missing trace_id entirely, or is field renamed? we had a few variants last quarter: trace_id vs traceId vs x_trace_id.

maya: missing. not renamed. payloads that hit the forwarder after batching just don't contain the attribute.

james: collector config change a few days ago toggled batch_compression and changed the attribute processor ordering. i suspect attribute processor runs before sampling now.

samir: ok if sampling is removing span attributes before enrichment, we need one of two fixes:
- move the log-enrichment processor to run earlier (pre-sampling)
- or change the forwarder to persist a minimal trace header even when spans are sampled out

eve: note: any change that adds trace ids to logs needs privacy review. some customers send PII in baggage. we should not auto-inject every baggage field into logs.

anna_k: agreed. proposal: the collector should add only the canonical trace_id (not baggage) and strip sensitive fields. config flag like `enrich.logs.with_trace_id_only = true`. defaults to true.

samir: that seems reasonable. also we should standardize the key to `trace.trace_id` in structured logs and the console joiner should accept aliases. avoids brittle searches.

maya: +1. Also we need a migration plan: we have historical logs using `traceId` and `x_trace_id`. If we switch to `trace.trace_id` all dashboards break.

james: we can do dual-write for a few weeks: collector adds both `trace.trace_id` and legacy keys when enabled. then update dashboards and saved searches, then turn off legacy key. do canary rollout to 10% of traffic.

samir: rollout checklist:
1) collector config change with `enrich.logs.with_trace_id_only=true` and `compat.keys=[traceId,x_trace_id]`
2) update console log ingestion docs + search suggestions
3) update dashboards (kpi teams) and send PRs to owners
4) canary 10% (monitor join rates, increases in console query latency)
5) 100% and legacy deprecate after 30 days

maya: one more: telemetry retention. when we add trace_id to logs, we may see more trace-based joins that increase query cost. do we have quotas/alerting on cross-dataset joins?

eve: we currently charge/track by ingested tokens for logs and by span count for traces. joins are free but they hit compute; we should add a cost estimate to the console when people run cross-joins and set a warning for large window queries.

anna_k: technically we can add a sampler on the query layer to limit cross-join results by default for non-admins. but ops needs to sign off.

james: infra-bot FYI: will create canary hosts for collector v2 with attribute reordering.

infra-bot: created canary cluster `collector-canary-7` in us-west1, 10% traffic routing ready. PR: infra/collector#842.

samir: great. next steps: anna to prepare collector config patch, maya to run sample log set through canary and validate trace linking, eve to draft privacy/playbook blurb for customers. I'll send a rollout calendar and owners.

maya: testing notes — i'll include a small script to synthesize OTLP spans + app logs showing both sampled and unsampled spans, and a grepable export so infra can assert trace_id present. will post results here in the canary window.

eve: thunk on retention: if customers rely on trace-linked logs for SLO analysis, they may want longer log retention. ops/product should add an opt-in retention tier for trace-linked workflows. cc @product.

samir: thanks all. keeping this thread for canary updates. please ping me if you find any mismatch between span.trace_id and log.trace.trace_id.

maya: noted — will post canary run at 2001122360 with sample outputs.

james: tagging follow-up: eng-platform/telemetry meeting tomorrow to finalize rollout window.

maya: thanks. :thumbsup:
